changes.title: Cross-device activity used for non-account personalization
changes.new_excerpt: whether to show you more relevant search results or ads based on your activity across devices
changes.old_excerpt: whether to show you more relevant search results or ads based on your activity
changes.explanation: The policy now states that for users not signed in to a Google Account, data tied to a browser, application, or device identifier may be used to personalize search results or ads based on activity tracked across multiple devices, rather than just within a single browsing session or device as previously described.
changes.practical_effect: Even without signing in, a user's activity on one device may be linked and used to influence search results or ads shown on another device.

report.summary: Google updated its Privacy Policy to clarify that for signed-out users, activity-based personalization of search results and ads may occur across multiple devices, not just within a single session or device.

report.cosmetic_note: The only changes are removal of "Learn more" hyperlink text from two example paragraphs about Google Photos and Google Trends; the substantive descriptions of how data is used remain unchanged.
report.summary: The changes consist solely of removing "Learn more" link labels from two illustrative examples, with no alteration to the underlying policy content.

changes.title: New Korea-specific PIPA addendum added
changes.new_excerpt: This section applies to the extent that Anthropic is subject to the Personal Information Protection Act ("PIPA")
changes.explanation: A new addendum has been added specifically for users in the Republic of Korea, supplementing the main Privacy Policy under Korea's Personal Information Protection Act. It states this addendum controls over the main policy in case of inconsistency for Korean users.
changes.practical_effect: Users in South Korea now have an additional, more detailed set of disclosures governing how their personal data is collected, used, and transferred, which takes precedence over the general policy where the two conflict.

changes.title: New disclosure of identity verification data collection
changes.new_excerpt: Purpose: Identity verification, Fraud and abuse monitoring
changes.explanation: The addendum newly discloses that Anthropic collects name, birthdate, sex, a native-foreigner code, and duplication information (DI) for identity verification and fraud/abuse monitoring purposes, retained until account deletion.
changes.practical_effect: Korean users are now informed that additional identity-related data is being collected and retained specifically for verification and fraud prevention until they delete their account.

changes.title: New disclosure of delegated data processing to third parties
changes.new_excerpt: Anthropic delegates the processing of personal data as described here and below, and the delegatees may process personal data according to the purpose of the…
changes.explanation: The addendum discloses that Anthropic delegates certain personal data processing tasks to named third parties: Korea Credit Bureau for fraud/identity verification and Kim & Chang for domestic representative duties.
changes.practical_effect: Users' data may be processed by these named third-party organizations for the stated purposes, in addition to Anthropic itself.

changes.title: New disclosure of overseas transfer of identity data to Persona (US)
changes.new_excerpt: Anthropic delegates the processing of personal data to affiliates and third parties, all of whom are located overseas.
changes.explanation: The addendum discloses that identity-verification data (name, birthdate, sex, native-foreigner code, DI) is transferred to Persona, a company located in the United States, for fraud detection and identity verification, retained for 3 years under a specific PIPA legal basis.
changes.practical_effect: Korean users' identity data may be sent to and stored by a US-based company for up to three years as part of identity verification processing.

changes.title: New right to object to overseas data transfer
changes.new_excerpt: You may have the right to request that your personal data not be transferred overseas as described above.
changes.explanation: The addendum newly informs users they may request that their data not be transferred overseas by contacting Anthropic's privacy email or Data Protection Officer, but warns this may limit Anthropic's ability to provide services.
changes.practical_effect: Users can attempt to opt out of overseas data transfer, but doing so may result in reduced or unavailable service functionality.

changes.title: Change of Korea domestic representative and contact details
changes.explanation: The domestic representative contact information for South Korea has changed from Bae, Kim & Lee LLC to Kim & Chang, including new phone number and email address.
changes.practical_effect: Users in South Korea seeking to contact the domestic representative about privacy matters must now use the new Kim & Chang contact details instead of the previous firm's contact information.

report.summary: Anthropic added a new Korea-specific PIPA addendum to its Privacy Policy detailing collection of identity-verification data, delegation of processing to third parties (Korea Credit Bureau, Kim & Chang), and overseas transfer of identity data to a US-based verification vendor (Persona), along with a user right to object to such transfers. The domestic representative in South Korea also changed from Bae, Kim & Lee LLC to Kim & Chang, with updated contact details."

report.cosmetic_note: All detected changes involve reordering of section labels/headings and navigation or page layout elements (e.g., menu labels, contact section headings, form-related text), with no changes to the substantive terms, rights, or obligations described in the policies.
report.summary: The changes consist solely of reformatting and relabeling of navigation/contact page elements; no substantive policy language was altered.

changes.title: Automatic sign-in via university single sign-on
changes.new_excerpt: the Platform may sign you in automatically. You can sign out at any time, and you will only be signed into an account
changes.explanation: The updated policy adds a new provision stating that if a user has an active single sign-on session with their university, the Platform may automatically log them in without a separate login step. It notes users can sign out and will only be signed into a pre-existing account.
changes.practical_effect: Users who are already logged into their university's single sign-on system may find themselves automatically signed into the Platform without taking any additional login action.

report.summary: The privacy policy adds a new section describing automatic sign-in through a user's university single sign-on session, noting users can sign out and will only access an existing account.
